note.explanation: Renewable sources are naturally replenished, while non-renewable sources are limited and can run out. Your textbook describes several sources of energy, including fossil fuels, water, sunlight, wind, tides, waves, biomass, nuclear fuels and heat from rocks inside Earth.
examples: Solar energy comes from sunlight and is renewable.
Fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas are non-renewable.
note.checkAnswer: Wind energy is renewable because wind is naturally replenished.
note.simple: Renewable energy sources are replaced naturally. Non-renewable sources are used up faster than nature can replace them.
note.checkQuestion: Is wind energy renewable or non-renewable? Give one reason.
note.title: Renewable and non-renewable energy
steps: Decide whether nature can replace the source in a relatively short time.
If it is naturally replenished, call it renewable.
If it is limited and can run out, call it non-renewable.
Give examples to support your answer.
note.answer: Renewable sources are naturally replenished; non-renewable sources are limited and can run out.

options: The burning fuel heats water to produce steam
The fuel directly turns the generator
The condenser burns the fuel
The transformer changes fuel into steam
mcqs.stem: In a fossil-fuel power station, what first uses the heat released by burning the fuel?
rationales: Correct: the heat is used to produce steam, which runs the turbine.
Incorrect: the steam turns the turbine, and the turbine runs the generator.
Incorrect: a condenser cools steam; it does not burn fuel.
Incorrect: a transformer changes voltage, not fuel into steam.

options: Chemical energy changes directly into electrical energy
Gravitational potential energy changes into kinetic energy as water falls
Nuclear energy changes into sound energy
Solar energy changes into gravitational potential energy
mcqs.stem: What energy change occurs when water falls from a high reservoir in hydroelectric generation?
rationales: Incorrect: this is not the energy change described for falling reservoir water.
Correct: stored gravitational potential energy changes into kinetic energy as the water falls.
Incorrect: nuclear energy is not involved in this process.
Incorrect: the reservoir water's stored energy is gravitational potential energy, not solar energy.

options: Solar cells are also called photovoltaic cells
Solar cells work only by boiling water
A single solar cell gives a very high voltage
Solar cells are connected in parallel to make voltage sufficient
mcqs.stem: Which statement about solar cells agrees with your textbook?
rationales: Correct: solar cells are also known as photovoltaic cells.
Incorrect: sunlight is transformed directly into electricity by solar cells; boiling water is another solar-energy method.
Incorrect: the voltage from a single voltaic cell is very low.
Incorrect: your textbook says many cells are connected in series to obtain sufficient voltage.

options: Coal
Uranium
Wind
Sunlight
mcqs.stem: Which material is named in your textbook as a nuclear fuel?
rationales: Incorrect: coal is a fossil fuel.
Correct: uranium is a nuclear fuel; plutonium is another example in the text.
Incorrect: wind is used to run wind generators, not as nuclear fuel.
Incorrect: sunlight is the source of solar energy.

options: Cold water is pumped underground, heated by hot rocks and returned as steam
Hot rocks are burned at the surface to make fuel
Wind drives water through the hot rocks
A dam traps water above the hot rocks
mcqs.stem: How is geothermal energy used to produce electricity in the method described in your textbook?
rationales: Correct: cold water is heated by underground hot rocks, and the resulting steam runs a generator.
Incorrect: the rocks provide heat underground; they are not burned as fuel at the surface.
Incorrect: wind is not the mechanism used in the geothermal process described.
Incorrect: the described method pumps water down a drilled hole; it does not require a dam above the rocks.

options: A single windmill is always sufficient for large-scale generation
A wind farm with a hundred or more windmills may be needed for large-scale generation
Windmills generate electricity by burning biomass
Wind generators need falling water to turn their turbines
mcqs.stem: What does your textbook say may be needed for large-scale wind power generation?
rationales: Incorrect: the text says a large wind farm may be needed.
Correct: a wind farm with a hundred or more windmills is given as the large-scale arrangement.
Incorrect: burning biomass is a separate energy method.
Incorrect: falling water is used in hydroelectric generation, not wind generation.

options: The Moon's gravitational force gives rise to tides
The Sun's heat makes the sea rise twice a day
Tides are caused by hot rocks beneath the sea
Tides are made by burning fossil fuels
mcqs.stem: According to your textbook, what gives rise to tides in the seas?
rationales: Correct: the textbook attributes tides to the gravitational force of the Moon.
Incorrect: the text does not say that the Sun's heat causes the tides.
Incorrect: hot rocks are associated with geothermal energy.
Incorrect: burning fossil fuels does not cause tides.

options: Micro-organisms break down biomass in the absence of oxygen
Biomass is frozen in a tank until it becomes methane
Biomass is mixed with steam in a turbine to make oxygen
Biomass is exposed to sunlight to produce coal
mcqs.stem: How is methane-rich biogas produced in a digester?
rationales: Correct: micro-organisms break down biomass in the absence of oxygen in the digester.
Incorrect: freezing biomass is not the method described.
Incorrect: the text describes breakdown without oxygen, not mixing biomass with steam to make oxygen.
Incorrect: sunlight does not turn biomass into coal in the described process.

explain.title: Fossil fuel energy
explain.body: Fossil fuel energy comes out from burning of oil, coal and natural gas. These materials are known as fossil fuels. Their burning gives out heat, which is used to generate steam. The steam runs turbines to produce electricity.

explain.title: Hydroelectric generation
explain.body: Hydroelectric generation is the electricity generated from the power of falling water. Water in a high lake or reservoir possesses gravitational potential energy stored in it. When water is allowed to fall from height, the potential energy is changed into kinetic energy. Running water rotates a turbine, which runs the electric generator.

explain.title: Solar energy
explain.body: The energy obtained from sunlight is referred to as solar energy. Solar cells, also known as photo voltaic cells, transform sunlight directly into electricity. A single cell gives very low voltage, so many cells are connected in series to form a solar cell panel.

explain.title: Geothermal energy
explain.body: This energy is known as geothermal energy which can be extracted to run electric generators. Cold water is pumped down to hot rocks, where it heats up and boils. The steam comes out through another hole and runs the generator.

explain.title: Biofuel energy
explain.body: It is that energy which is obtained from the biomass. Biomass consists of organic materials such as plants, waste foods, animals dung, sewage, etc. In a digester, micro-organisms break down biomass in the absence of oxygen to produce methane-rich biogas.

mistakes: Do not confuse renewable with unlimited: explain that a renewable source is naturally replenished.
Do not call coal, oil or natural gas renewable; they are fossil fuels.
For hydroelectricity, do not skip the energy change from gravitational potential energy to kinetic energy.
Do not say a single solar cell provides high voltage; your textbook says many cells are connected in series for sufficient voltage.
Do not mix up the roles of a turbine, generator and transformer: running water or steam turns the turbine, the generator produces electricity, and a transformer changes voltage.
